safe_temperature.disagreements: The FDA standard mandates a minimum internal temperature of 145°F (with a 3-minute rest period) for whole lamb cuts (chops, roasts, steaks) and 160°F for ground lamb. Culinary and precision cooking sources in the notebook depart from this for specific cuts and culinary results: Fit Foodie Finds sous-vide guidance recommends water bath temperatures of 118°F to 120°F (rare to medium-rare) for lamb chops, followed by a rapid 30-60 second per side sear; grilling and pan-searing guides for tender fillet steaks target 130°F–135°F for medium-rare before resting, noting that 145°F yields medium to medium-well doneness; conversely, slow-roasting and braising methods for tough, collagen-heavy cuts (shoulder and leg) deliberately cook meat far beyond 145°F to internal temperatures of 195°F–205°F to melt connective tissue into shreddable, fork-tender meat.

avoid.warning: Time-temperature abuse during resting: Leaving cooked meat at room temperature between 40°F and 140°F (the Temperature Danger Zone) for longer than 2 hours creates significant bacterial growth risks.

methods.heat: 390°F (200°C) initial blast for 15 minutes, then reduced to 350°F (180°C)
methods.time: 1 hour 15 minutes to 1 hour 30 minutes for a 5 to 6 lb leg
methods.doneness: 135°F (57°C) internal temperature for medium-rare before resting, rising to 145°F (63°C)
methods.rest: 15 to 20 minutes loosely tented with foil
methods.tips: Rest the roast directly on a bed of halved onions and garlic bulbs to keep it elevated off the pan and to infuse the pan drippings for gravy; baste occasionally with pan juices.

methods.time: 2.5 to 3 hours covered, plus 20 to 25 minutes uncovered for a 3.5 to 4 lb shoulder
methods.doneness: Fork-tender, meat easily shreds away from the bone (internal temperature 195°F–205°F)
methods.rest: 10 to 15 minutes before carving or pulling
methods.tips: Slow-braise with dry white wine or rich broth and aromatic Herbes de Provence in a heavy lidded Dutch oven or foil-sealed roasting pan to melt connective tissue into rich pan juices.

methods.heat: 118°F to 120°F (48°C–49°C) water bath, then smoking-hot cast-iron skillet
